channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Galveston jury returns guilty verdict for Houston woman accused of throwing child from hotel balcony
item.description: Channel Yonko received an automatic life sentence after being convicted Friday of killing her 17-month-old daughter in 2024. Court records show her defense attorney subsequently filed a notice of appeal.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (March 6, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Ramadan display removed from Houston elementary school for violating ‘religious neutrality’ policy
item.description: Spring Branch ISD officials say they ordered Bunker Hill Elementary to remove decorations celebrating the Muslim holiday after a parent expressed concern the display did not align with district policy. Some say other religious displays were previously allowed.

item.title: Galveston gears up for hundreds of thousands of visitors as spring break begins
item.description: Officials say the island could see anywhere from 200,000-300,000 visitors from March 9-20, when most Texas schools have their spring break vacations.

item.title: Rice University’s Kinder Institute receives $55 million grant for continued research
item.description: The donation from the Kinder Foundation includes $50 million for the institute’s endowment, allowing the research center to continue operating for decades, Rice University said.

item.title: Texas sees record voter turnout in primaries, led by Democratic voters
item.description: Democratic voters in the state outnumbered Republican voters by nearly 7% in Tuesday's primary election, a shift from the election cycles in 2022 and 2024, based on unofficial numbers from the Texas Secretary of State's Office.

item.title: Plane from Houston that crashed in Maine spent more time on runway than recommended after deicing, NTSB says
item.description: The four passengers and two pilots had stopped to refuel in Bangor as they traveled from Houston to France on Jan. 25. The passengers included Houston lawyer Tara Arnold, 46, and three people who worked for her luxury travel company.

item.title: Harris County chief medical examiner Luis Sanchez announces resignation after decades-long tenure
item.description: Sanchez was appointed to the role by county commissioners in 2002. He is credited for sustaining the office's national accreditations and navigating it through the COVID-19 pandemic, which claimed the lives of more than 8,000 Harris County residents.

item.title: Walkable suspended labyrinth exhibit returns to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
item.description: "Ernesto Neto: SunForceOceanLife," a 35-foot structure with walkable pathways, is back on view until September after originally being commissioned for MFAH in 2019.
